chapters.title: The Righteous Judgment of God
chapters.html:
2 Thessalonians 1

1Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:

2Grace to you and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

Endurance in Persecution

3We ought always to thank God for you, brothers, as is right, because your faith is growing greatly and the love of every one of you for one another is increasing,

4so that we ourselves boast about you in the churches of God for your endurance and faith in all your persecutions and the troubles you are bearing.

5This is evidence of the righteous judgment of God, so that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you are suffering,

6since it is right in God's sight to repay with trouble those who trouble you,

7and to give relief to you who are troubled, and to us as well, when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with His mighty angels

8in flaming fire, bringing vengeance on those who do not know God and on those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus.

9They will pay the penalty of eternal destruction, away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of His might,

10when He comes on that day to be glorified in His saints and to be marveled at among all who have believed, because our testimony to you was believed.

11To this end we always pray for you, that our God may make you worthy of His calling and fulfill by His power every desire for goodness and every work of faith,

12so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in Him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

chapters.title: The Man of Lawlessness
chapters.html:
2 Thessalonians 2

1Now about the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our being gathered together to Him, we ask you, brothers,

2not to be quickly shaken in mind or alarmed, whether by a spirit or by a word or by a letter seeming to be from us, saying that the day of the Lord has already come.

3Let no one deceive you in any way. For that day will not come unless the falling away comes first, and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction,

4who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or object of worship, so that he takes his seat in the temple of God, proclaiming himself to be God.

5Do you not remember that when I was still with you I told you these things?

6You know what is restraining him now, so that he may be revealed in his own time.

7For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only he who now restrains it will do so until he is taken out of the way.

8Then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of His mouth and bring to nothing by the appearing of His coming.

9The coming of the lawless one is by the working of Satan, with every kind of power and false signs and wonders,

10and with every kind of wicked deception for those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth so as to be saved.

11For this reason God sends them a working of delusion, so that they believe the lie,

12so that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in wickedness.

Stand Firm

13But we ought always to thank God for you, brothers loved by the Lord, because God chose you as firstfruits for salvation, through the holiness the Spirit gives and through belief in the truth.

14To this He called you through our gospel, so that you may obtain the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.

15So then, brothers, stand firm and hold to the traditions you were taught by us, whether by word of mouth or by our letter.

16Now may our Lord Jesus Christ Himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope by grace,

17comfort your hearts and strengthen them in every good work and word.

Notes

  • vv4, 8 "exalts himself above every so-called god… whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of His mouth" — two prophecies. The king of Daniel's last vision will exalt himself and magnify himself above every god (Daniel 11:36). And the shoot of Jesse with the breath of his lips… will kill the wicked (Isaiah 11:4), in the Greek en pneumati… anelei, the verb Paul uses here, anelei. What Isaiah said of the coming king, Paul says of the Lord Jesus.

  • vv6–7 "what is restraining him… he who now restrains it" — to katechon, a thing, and ho katechōn, a person. The Thessalonians know what it is, and Paul does not say. The letter gives no more than that something, and someone, holds the lawless one back until a set time.

chapters.title: Do Not Grow Weary
chapters.html:
2 Thessalonians 3

Pray for Us

1Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may run its course and be glorified, as it was among you,

2and that we may be rescued from wicked and evil men; for not all have faith.

3But the Lord is faithful. He will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.

4We have confidence in the Lord about you, that you are doing and will do what we command.

5May the Lord direct your hearts to the love of God and to the endurance of Christ.

Against Idleness

6We command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to keep away from any brother who is walking in idleness and not according to the tradition you received from us.

7For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we were not idle when we were with you,

8and we did not eat anyone's bread without paying for it, but with labor and toil we worked night and day, so as not to be a burden to any of you.

9It was not that we do not have the right, but to give you ourselves as an example to imitate.

10For even when we were with you, we gave you this command: if anyone is not willing to work, let him not eat.

11For we hear that some among you are walking in idleness, not busy at work but busybodies.

12Such people we command and urge in the Lord Jesus Christ to work quietly and earn their own bread.

13As for you, brothers, do not grow weary in doing good.

14If anyone does not obey what we say in this letter, take note of that person and have nothing to do with him, so that he may be ashamed.

15Do not regard him as an enemy, but warn him as a brother.

Benediction

16Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace at all times in every way. The Lord be with you all.

17I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. This is the mark in every letter; this is how I write.

18The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all.
